h: רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ אִיָּר, א׳ Rosh Chodesh Iyar, 1

p: It is stated in the Gemara (Rosh Hashanah 11a):
From where do we know that the Avos were born in Nissan?
"And it was..." in the month of Ziv,
the month in which were born
the radiant ones of the world.
they had already been born, in Nissan.
This needs explanation: according to this,
why is the month of Iyar called Ziv?
Since they were born in Nissan,
הֲוָה לֵיהּ לִקְרוֹת חוֹדֶשׁ נִיסָן זִיו
the month of Nissan should have been called Ziv!
as we have said many times,
that the main light of the month
And for this reason it is called "Rosh Chodesh,"
and not "the first of the month" —
because it is the head of the month,
and everything follows after the head.
And since the Avos were born
is called the month of Ziv.
after all, the months are reckoned
אַךְ הַחוֹדֶשׁ הַזֶּה לָכֶם רֹאשׁ חֳדָשִׁים
But "This month shall be for you the head of the months" —
counting by the months of the moon —
was first instituted at Yetzias Mitzrayim,
when the Jewish nation was founded;
since they counted by the sun then;
when the Jewish nation came into being,
the month of Iyar was called Ziv,
the light of the Avos was already present.
And all the Avos are the light of the sun,
that was created on the first day,
"'Let there be light' — this is Avraham."
And the primordial light was created
מִסּוֹף הָעוֹלָם וְעַד סוֹפוֹ (חֲגִיגָה יב, א)
from one end of the world to the other (Chagigah 12a).
Afterwards, when it was hidden away
and the luminaries were created on the fourth day,
the light of the sun receives
and the moon receives from the light of the sun.
As it says of the future (Yeshayahu 30:26):
"And the light of the moon shall be like the light of the sun,
and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold,
like the light of the seven days."
"like the light of the seven days" —
which comes to three hundred forty-three
וְהַשֶּׁמֶשׁ הוּא חֵלֶק קָטָן מֵאוֹר הָרִאשׁוֹן
and the sun is only a small part of the primordial light.
it is stated in the Midrash (Bereishis Rabbah 95:3):
And the essence of light is the Torah,
as it says (Mishlei 6:23), "And Torah is light."
is written in the utterance "Let there be light"
correspond to the five Chumashim of the Torah
the sun has come, the sun has come, etc.
Who revealed to him that my name is Sun?"
וְזֶה עִנְיַן מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ו, ט)
And this is the meaning of what Chazal said (Bereishis Rabbah 6:9),
are you not my father's purchase?
לֹא כָּךְ רָאָה אוֹתְךָ אַבָּא בַּחֲלוֹם
Did not my father see you so in a dream:
what kind of claim is it
that the one likened to the sun
for whose sake the primordial light was hidden away,
as stated in the Zohar HaKadosh
זָרַע לֵיהּ קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וְכוּלֵּי
the Holy One, blessed be He, sowed it...
who is the gardener of the garden...
And the sun receives its light
that is hidden away for the tzaddikim.
And this is what Yehoshua said to the sun:
which is the "light sown for the tzaddik."
the sun receives from this light,
and the moon receives from the light of the sun.
And this is why it is called the month of Ziv:
when the Jewish nation was formed,
the light of the Avos was already present.
that the Avos were born in Tishrei,
because it has radiance for the trees.
We need to understand the reason
by the name Ziv in the pasuk,
for in the pesukim we do not find
since the names of the months came up from Bavel
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּירוּשַׁלְמִי רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה א, ב
Only regarding the building of the Beis HaMikdash
Now Tishrei, "the month of the Eisanim" —
which the Gemara (Rosh Hashanah ibid.) explains
means they are strong in mitzvos —
it is understandable to give it a special name.
why was it given the special name Ziv
are the words of the Living God,"
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (דְּבָרִים כ, יט)
in the way of what is said (Devarim 20:19):
"For man is a tree of the field."
And in the Midrash (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:17):
To a prince who recovered from his illness.
His tutor said to the king,
עֲדַיִין לֹא בָּא בְּנִי לְזִיווֹ וְכוּלֵּי
"My son has not yet regained his radiance..."
there were among them people with blemishes
from the bondage of mortar and bricks...
The Holy One, blessed be He, said to them:
עֲדַיִין לֹא בָּא זִיוָתָן שֶׁל בָּנַי
"My children's radiance has not yet returned
from the bondage of mortar and bricks.
Let My children be refreshed for three months,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ אֶתֵּן לָהֶם הַתּוֹרָה וְכוּלֵּי
and afterwards I will give them the Torah..."
that Yisrael were healed until Matan Torah,
when all those with blemishes were healed,
מִנַּיִן שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בָּהֶן סוּמִין וְכוּלֵּי
"From where do we know there were no blind among them...
that there were no deaf among them..."
And the Torah is "healing to all his flesh,"
אֵין צָרִיךְ זְמַן שְׁלֹשָׁה חֳדָשִׁים לְרַפְּאוֹתָן
does not need three months to heal them;
"And the Egyptians did evil to us" —
to the point that it says (ibid. 4:34),
"a nation from the midst of a nation,"
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה כג, ב)
as stated in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah 23:2);
and they needed to be purified
עֲדַיִין לֹא בָּא זִיוָתָן שֶׁל בָּנַי
"My children's radiance has not yet come,"
from when it puts forth its blossom
they received in the month of Sivan,
was the preparation for Matan Torah.
And this is what they meant:
that the radiance of My children would come.
the month of Iyar is called Ziv,
because it has radiance for the trees —
"man is a tree of the field."
And although the time when the trees blossom
is in the days of Nissan
was the time of Yetzias Mitzrayim,
and likewise the Avos were born in Nissan —
the month of Iyar was given to them
as the one that brings the radiance of My children.
at the time the Beis HaMikdash was built,
it was called the month of Ziv.
For in truth the building of the Beis HaMikdash
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה א, ה
"And the House, when it was built" (Melachim I 6:7) —
which is the desire of the heart
that the revelation of the primordial light
was the beginning of the preparation,
in the month of Iyar before Sivan,
the month in which they received the Torah.
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ב, ה)
And about this he said (Shir HaShirim 2:5),
that they are still sick with love.
And he said, "Sustain me with ashishos,"
and it is stated in the Midrash (ibid. 2:16):
the Written Torah and the Oral Torah."
of the Written Torah it is written (Devarim 33:2),
"From His right hand, a fiery law for them";
and of the Oral Torah, too,
And it is expounded (end of Chagigah, 27a):
talmidei chachamim, whose whole body is fire
The intent is to the two explanations
of ashishah found in the Gemara (Pesachim 36b):
who said ashisha is a jug of wine,
וְכֵן בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג מ, א)
And likewise in the Zohar HaKadosh (III 40a):
And this is what they said (in the Midrash ibid.):
the Written Torah, the Oral Torah,"
(בְּרַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא, זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רעא, ב)
this is the bread of the Written Torah,
and the wine of the Oral Torah."
"and drink of the wine I have mixed,"
and it does not say "of My wine,"
by the Holy One, blessed be He, into the heart of Yisrael,
so that it seems as though they innovate it on their own;
and these are "My words which I have placed in your mouth"
And this is what they said:
these are the two explanations of ashishah.
Afterwards it says (in the Midrash ibid.):
that is, the light of the Oral Torah;
whose fragrance and taste are like apples."
This is "the secret of Hashem is for those who fear Him,"
which is the light felt in the heart,
"Her husband is known in the gates,"
וְאָמַר בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א קג, ב)
the One Who spoke and the world came into being,
אַתָּה מַכִּיר אֶת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְכוּלֵּי
you come to recognize the Holy One, blessed be He..."
for there had not yet come
And so too the preparation came
through the holiness of the Avos,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג מ, א)
as stated in the Zohar HaKadosh (III 40a):
Likewise at the third meal of Shabbos,
שֶׁהִיא סְעוּדָתָא דְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
which is the meal of Yaakov Avinu, alav hashalom,
we say (in the zemer Bnei Heichala),
"to behold the radiance of Ze'eir Anpin."
And likewise in the Midrash Rabbah
when he left there, its radiance departed..."
all the Avos are the primordial light,
but the merit of one tzaddik
And these and these are the words of the Living God:
for this reason it is called Ziv —
which is the month before Sivan,
and in it is the preparation for Matan Torah;
And then the radiance of Yisrael came
"to purify us from our klipos and our impurities."
And in it is the holiness of the Avos,
who too are the primordial light,
And so it is stated in Sefer Yetzirah
that this month was created with the letter vav,
שֶׁנִּקְרָא בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג ב, א)
which is called in the Zohar HaKadosh (III 2a)
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג קכב, ב)
and as stated in the Zohar HaKadosh (III 122b),
that the letter vav of the Holy Name —
וּמִינָּהּ יֵיעוּל עַל פּוּמָא דְּבַר נָשׁ
"from it there enter into a person's mouth
and vav-heh are Torah and mitzvah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם אַחַר כָּךְ (קכג, ב)
And although the essence of the Torah
